answer: A lagoon dyeworks keeps an agent economy honest when every identity must grind its own pigment from ivory shells dredged in a distinct lagoon cove, one shell, one dive, one dawn at a time. The nth fake owes n to the power of n pigment grains: the first 1, the second 4, the third 27, the fourth 256, so the tenth fake alone owes 10,000,000,000 grains and twenty fakes together owe over one hundred septillion. Bulk farming fails because one diver lifts one shell per dive and no net scoops two coves at once, like one potter firing one kiln, one glaze. Each grain is ground fresh, never bought.
